days.name: Monday · Observe & Ask
days.lesson: Introduce **Final Systems Expedition**. Weather systems emerge from energy transfer, air motion, moisture, pressure, and interacting hazards.
days.lab: Complete a cumulative systems-analysis and engineering challenge.
worksheet: Write or draw what you already notice about final systems expedition.
Record one observation related to time-stamped observations, counts, categories, or measurements.
Write one question you want to answer this week.

days.name: Tuesday · Measure & Record
days.lesson: Scientists make fair comparisons by recording the same kind of evidence. This week, focus on time-stamped observations, counts, categories, or measurements.
days.lab: Repeat or extend the week's investigation: Complete a cumulative systems-analysis and engineering challenge. Record at least two observations or measurements.
worksheet: Create a small data table with labels and units or categories.
Circle the largest change or most important difference.
Write one sentence describing what the data show.

days.name: Wednesday · Model & Explain
days.lesson: Use a model, diagram, or sequence to explain the idea: Weather systems emerge from energy transfer, air motion, moisture, pressure, and interacting hazards.
days.lab: Build, draw, or revise a model of final systems expedition using the week's evidence.
worksheet: Label your model with at least two of these words: weather, pressure, energy.
Draw arrows or numbers to show change, motion, or order when appropriate.
Explain one way the model is similar to real weather and one way it is different.

days.name: Thursday · Apply & Explore
days.lesson: Connect final systems expedition to a real forecast, weather map, local observation, or Solanar learning tool.
days.lab: Use **NAIB Mentor** or a teacher-provided weather source to find one example connected to this week's topic.
worksheet: Write the place, date/time, and source you used.
Record one piece of evidence from the source.
Explain how the evidence connects to this week's concept.
